resources.title: Housing — Adelaide
resources.body: Adelaide is one of Australia's more affordable capital cities. A 1-bedroom apartment in the city centre typically rents for approximately AUD 350–450 per week. South Australia's Residential Tenancies Act caps the bond at 4 weeks rent. Primary rental portals are realestate.com.au and domain.com.au.

resources.title: Banking — Adelaide
resources.body: To open a bank account in Australia, new arrivals typically need a valid passport, proof of Australian address, and a Tax File Number (TFN). CommBank allows account opening up to 14 days before arrival. ANZ and NAB also serve new residents.

resources.title: Schools & childcare — Adelaide
resources.body: Adelaide has international schools offering IB and other curricula. The national school directory myschool.edu.au lists all South Australian schools. State schools fall under the SA Department for Education.

resources.title: Registration & admin — Adelaide
resources.body: Visa holders in Australia must notify the Department of Home Affairs of any address changes. New residents should register with myGov (my.gov.au) to link ATO, Medicare, and Centrelink services.

resources.title: Tax & finance — Adelaide
resources.body: All workers and income earners in Australia require a Tax File Number (TFN) from the Australian Taxation Office (ATO). Apply online for free at ato.gov.au.

resources.title: Transport — Adelaide
resources.body: Adelaide public transport is operated by Adelaide Metro using the Metrocard (or contactless payments). The network covers buses, trains, and trams. A 28-day (monthly) Metrocard pass price is not retrievable from currently accessible pages. Overseas licence holders must convert to an SA licence via Service SA. Medicare registration via Services Australia.

resources.title: Housing — Brisbane
resources.body: Brisbane's 1-bedroom apartment in the city centre typically rents for approximately AUD 450–550 per week. Queensland's Residential Tenancies Act caps the bond at 4 weeks rent. Primary rental portals are realestate.com.au and domain.com.au.

resources.title: Banking — Brisbane
resources.body: To open a bank account in Australia, new arrivals typically need a valid passport, proof of Australian address, and a Tax File Number (TFN). CommBank allows account opening up to 14 days before arrival. ANZ and NAB also serve new residents. In-branch ID verification within 20 days of opening is required by CommBank.

resources.title: Schools & childcare — Brisbane
resources.body: Brisbane has international schools offering IB, British, and American curricula. The national school directory myschool.edu.au lists all Queensland schools. Queensland state schools fall under the Department of Education Queensland (qed.qld.gov.au).

resources.title: Registration & admin — Brisbane
resources.body: Visa holders in Australia must notify the Department of Home Affairs of any address changes. New residents should register with myGov (my.gov.au) to link ATO, Medicare, and Centrelink services.

resources.title: Tax & finance — Brisbane
resources.body: All workers and income earners in Australia require a Tax File Number (TFN) from the Australian Taxation Office (ATO). Apply online for free at ato.gov.au.

resources.title: Transport — Brisbane
resources.body: Brisbane public transport is operated by Translink (Queensland Government) using the go card or contactless payments. As of 2024, Queensland introduced a 50-cent flat fare across all Translink services, regardless of distance. Overseas licence holders may drive in Queensland on a foreign licence; upon becoming a resident, conversion to a Queensland licence via TMR is required. Medicare registration for eligible visa holders via Services Australia.

resources.title: Housing — Canberra
resources.body: Canberra is Australia's capital with a tight rental market. A 1-bedroom apartment in the city centre typically rents for approximately AUD 450–550 per week. ACT's Residential Tenencies Act caps the bond at 4 weeks rent. Primary rental portals are realestate.com.au and domain.com.au.

resources.title: Banking — Canberra
resources.body: To open a bank account in Australia, new arrivals typically need a valid passport, proof of Australian address, and a Tax File Number (TFN). CommBank allows account opening up to 14 days before arrival. ANZ and NAB also serve new residents.

resources.title: Schools & childcare — Canberra
resources.body: Canberra has international schools including IB-curriculum institutions. The national school directory myschool.edu.au lists all ACT schools. ACT state schools fall under the ACT Education Directorate.

resources.title: Registration & admin — Canberra
resources.body: Visa holders in Australia must notify the Department of Home Affairs of any address changes. New residents should register with myGov (my.gov.au) to link ATO, Medicare, and Centrelink services.

resources.title: Tax & finance — Canberra
resources.body: All workers and income earners in Australia require a Tax File Number (TFN) from the Australian Taxation Office (ATO). Apply online for free at ato.gov.au. The ATO is headquartered in Canberra.

resources.title: Transport — Canberra
resources.body: Canberra public transport is operated by Transport Canberra using the MyWay+ card system. The network covers buses and the light rail (Canberra Metro). Monthly pass pricing was not retrievable from currently accessible pages. Overseas licence holders in ACT must convert to an ACT licence via Access Canberra. Medicare registration via Services Australia.

resources.title: Housing — Darwin
resources.body: Numbeo reports an August 2026 average of AUD 2,500 per month for a one-bedroom city-centre apartment: https://www.numbeo.com/cost-of-living/in/Darwin. Northern Territory guidance caps the security deposit at four weeks' rent, represented here as 1 month: https://nt.gov.au/property/private-renters/find-out-about-rental-costs/security-deposits-bonds. Domain provides Darwin City rental listings: https://www.domain.com.au/rent/darwin-city-nt-0800/.

resources.title: Banking — Darwin
resources.body: CommBank's migrant account page requires a current passport, entry-visa information, foreign tax-residency TINs, and an Australian residential address for full access after in-branch identification: https://www.commbank.com.au/moving-to-australia/banking.html. Westpac's official new-arrivals page supports Westpac as a newcomer option and asks for a mobile number, email, arrival date, Australian address, foreign tax number, and valid ID for activation: https://www.westpac.com.au/international-travel/new-to-australia/choice-new-arrivals/.

resources.title: Schools & childcare — Darwin
resources.body: Good Shepherd Lutheran College in the Darwin area states that it is an IB World School offering the International Baccalaureate Primary Years Programme: https://goodshepherd.nt.edu.au/our-schools. The Northern Territory Government's Darwin-region list links to the official education directory for government and non-government schools: https://nt.gov.au/learning/primary-and-secondary-students/list-of-urban-and-remote-schools.

resources.title: Registration & admin — Darwin
resources.body: On arrival, travellers must show a valid passport or travel document and complete and show an Incoming Passenger Card; the card requirement applies to most passengers, subject to prescribed exemptions: https://www.abf.gov.au/entering-and-leaving-australia/crossing-the-border/at-the-border/incoming-passenger-card-(ipc).

resources.title: Tax & finance — Darwin
resources.body: The Australian tax identifier is the Tax File Number (TFN). A permanent migrant or temporary visitor who is in Australia with a valid work-rights visa linked to their passport or travel document can apply online through Individual Auto-Registration; the ATO specifies alternative resident or paper routes when IAR is unavailable: https://www.ato.gov.au/individuals-and-families/tax-file-number/apply-for-a-tfn/foreign-passport-holders-permanent-migrants-and-temporary-visitors-tfn-application.

resources.title: Transport — Darwin
resources.body: CDC Northern Territory operates public bus services in Darwin, Palmerston and rural areas for the Northern Territory Government: https://cdcnorthernterritory.com.au/travel-info/timetables-and-maps/. NT Government says Greater Darwin public buses are currently free, so no monthly-pass fare is published: https://nt.gov.au/driving/public-transport-cycling/public-buses/fares. New NT residents must transfer an overseas licence within 3 months; recognised-country licences can transfer without theory and practical tests, while others must complete those tests: https://nt.gov.au/driving/licence/new-nt-residents-and-visitors/transfer-your-overseas-licence. Eligible Australian permanent residents can enrol in Medicare online through myGov or with the enrolment form and need to live in Australia, hold a current passport or ImmiCard, and have valid Home Affairs visa details: https://www.servicesaustralia.gov.au/enrolling-medicare-if-youre-australian-permanent-resident?context=60092.

resources.title: Housing — Gold Coast
resources.body: Gold Coast is a popular coastal city in QLD. A 1-bedroom apartment in the city centre (Surfers Paradise area) typically rents for approximately AUD 450–550 per week. Queensland's Residential Tenancies Act caps the bond at 4 weeks rent. Primary rental portals are realestate.com.au and domain.com.au.

resources.title: Banking — Gold Coast
resources.body: To open a bank account in Australia, new arrivals typically need a valid passport, proof of Australian address, and a Tax File Number (TFN). CommBank allows account opening up to 14 days before arrival. ANZ and NAB also serve new residents.

resources.title: Schools & childcare — Gold Coast
resources.body: The Gold Coast has international and IB schools. The national school directory myschool.edu.au lists all QLD schools in the Gold Coast area. State schools are under the Queensland Department of Education.

resources.title: Registration & admin — Gold Coast
resources.body: Visa holders in Australia must notify the Department of Home Affairs of any address changes. New residents should register with myGov (my.gov.au) to link ATO, Medicare, and Centrelink services.

resources.title: Tax & finance — Gold Coast
resources.body: All workers and income earners in Australia require a Tax File Number (TFN) from the Australian Taxation Office (ATO). Apply online for free at ato.gov.au.

resources.title: Transport — Gold Coast
resources.body: Gold Coast public transport is operated by Translink (Queensland Government) using the go card or contactless payments. As of 2024, Queensland introduced a 50-cent flat fare across all Translink services network-wide. The Gold Coast Light Rail (G:link) is included in the Translink network. Overseas licence holders in QLD must convert to a Queensland licence via TMR upon taking up residency. Medicare registration via Services Australia.

resources.title: Housing — Hobart
resources.body: Hobart, Tasmania's capital, has seen significant rental price rises. A 1-bedroom apartment in the city centre typically rents for approximately AUD 350–450 per week. Tasmania's Residential Tenancy Act caps the bond at 4 weeks rent. Primary rental portals are realestate.com.au and domain.com.au.

resources.title: Banking — Hobart
resources.body: To open a bank account in Australia, new arrivals typically need a valid passport, proof of Australian address, and a Tax File Number (TFN). CommBank allows account opening up to 14 days before arrival. ANZ and NAB also serve new residents.

resources.title: Schools & childcare — Hobart
resources.body: Hobart has public and private schools; IB programmes are offered at select institutions. The national school directory myschool.edu.au lists all Tasmanian schools. State schools are under the Tasmanian Department of Education, Children and Young People.

resources.title: Registration & admin — Hobart
resources.body: Visa holders in Australia must notify the Department of Home Affairs of any address changes. New residents should register with myGov (my.gov.au) to link ATO, Medicare, and Centrelink services.

resources.title: Tax & finance — Hobart
resources.body: All workers and income earners in Australia require a Tax File Number (TFN) from the Australian Taxation Office (ATO). Apply online for free at ato.gov.au.

resources.title: Transport — Hobart
resources.body: Hobart public transport is operated by Metro Tasmania (bus network only; no rail or light rail). Fare pricing was not retrievable from currently accessible official pages. Overseas licence holders in Tasmania must convert to a Tasmanian licence via Service Tasmania within 3 months of taking up residency. Medicare registration via Services Australia.

resources.title: Housing — Melbourne
resources.body: Melbourne's inner-city 1-bedroom apartment typically rents for approximately AUD 500–600 per week. Victoria's Residential Tenancies Act sets the bond (deposit) at a maximum of 1 month's rent (approximately 4 weeks). Primary rental portals are realestate.com.au and domain.com.au.

resources.title: Banking — Melbourne
resources.body: To open a bank account in Australia, new arrivals typically need a valid passport, proof of Australian address, and a Tax File Number (TFN). CommBank allows account opening up to 14 days before arrival and accepts new migrants within 12 months of arrival with in-branch ID verification. ANZ offers the ANZ Access Advantage account for new residents with a $5 monthly fee waivable on $2,000+ monthly deposits.

resources.title: Schools & childcare — Melbourne
resources.body: Melbourne has numerous international schools offering IB, British, and American curricula. The national directory myschool.edu.au lists all schools. VIC state schools fall under the Department of Education. Notable international-curriculum schools include Haileybury, Carey Baptist Grammar, and the French School (ACFE-affiliated).

resources.title: Registration & admin — Melbourne
resources.body: Visa holders in Australia must notify the Department of Home Affairs of any address changes. New residents should register with myGov (my.gov.au) to link ATO, Medicare, and Centrelink services.

resources.title: Tax & finance — Melbourne
resources.body: All workers and income earners in Australia require a Tax File Number (TFN) from the Australian Taxation Office (ATO). Apply online for free at ato.gov.au. The TFN is required by employers for payroll tax withholding.

resources.title: Transport — Melbourne
resources.body: Melbourne's public transport is operated by Public Transport Victoria (PTV) using the myki card system. The network covers metropolitan trains, trams, and buses. A 28-day (monthly) myki Pass for Zone 1+2 (full metro network) costs approximately AUD 181.60. Overseas licence holders visiting Victoria may drive on their foreign licence; those taking up residence must convert to a Victorian licence via VicRoads. Medicare registration for eligible visa holders is via Services Australia.

resources.title: Housing — Newcastle
resources.body: Newcastle (NSW) is more affordable than Sydney. A 1-bedroom apartment in the city centre typically rents for approximately AUD 350–430 per week. NSW's Residential Tenancies Act caps the bond at 4 weeks rent. Primary rental portals are realestate.com.au and domain.com.au.

resources.title: Banking — Newcastle
resources.body: To open a bank account in Australia, new arrivals typically need a valid passport, proof of Australian address, and a Tax File Number (TFN). CommBank allows account opening up to 14 days before arrival. ANZ and NAB also serve new residents.

resources.title: Schools & childcare — Newcastle
resources.body: Newcastle has a range of public and private schools; IB programmes are available at select schools. The national school directory myschool.edu.au lists all NSW schools in the Newcastle region. State schools are under the NSW Department of Education.

resources.title: Registration & admin — Newcastle
resources.body: Visa holders in Australia must notify the Department of Home Affairs of any address changes. New residents should register with myGov (my.gov.au) to link ATO, Medicare, and Centrelink services.

resources.title: Tax & finance — Newcastle
resources.body: All workers and income earners in Australia require a Tax File Number (TFN) from the Australian Taxation Office (ATO). Apply online for free at ato.gov.au.

resources.title: Transport — Newcastle
resources.body: Newcastle public transport is operated by Transport for NSW using the Opal card. The network includes buses and the Newcastle Light Rail. Fares are distance-based using the Opal system with daily and weekly caps. Overseas licence holders in NSW must exchange to an NSW licence via Service NSW upon becoming a NSW resident. Medicare registration via Services Australia.

resources.title: Housing — Perth
resources.body: Perth's 1-bedroom apartment in the city centre typically rents for approximately AUD 450–550 per week. Western Australia's Residential Tenancies Act caps the bond at 4 weeks rent. Primary rental portals are realestate.com.au and domain.com.au.

resources.title: Banking — Perth
resources.body: To open a bank account in Australia, new arrivals typically need a valid passport, proof of Australian address, and a Tax File Number (TFN). CommBank allows account opening up to 14 days before arrival. ANZ and NAB also serve new residents.

resources.title: Schools & childcare — Perth
resources.body: Perth has international schools offering IB and British curricula. The national school directory myschool.edu.au lists all WA schools. WA state schools fall under the Department of Education WA.

resources.title: Registration & admin — Perth
resources.body: Visa holders in Australia must notify the Department of Home Affairs of any address changes. New residents should register with myGov (my.gov.au) to link ATO, Medicare, and Centrelink services.

resources.title: Tax & finance — Perth
resources.body: All workers and income earners in Australia require a Tax File Number (TFN) from the Australian Taxation Office (ATO). Apply online for free at ato.gov.au.

resources.title: Transport — Perth
resources.body: Perth public transport is operated by Transperth using the SmartRider card. Standard adult fares as of January 2026: 2-section (up to 3.2 km) AUD $2.40 cash / $1.92 SmartRider (20% discount with registered autoload); Go Anywhere (3-hour system-wide) AUD $3.50 cash / $2.80 SmartRider (20% discount); DayRider $7.00. Sundays are free for SmartRider/contactless holders. No monthly pass; DayRider provides unlimited daily travel. Overseas licence holders in WA must convert to a WA driver's licence via the Department of Transport. Medicare registration via Services Australia.

resources.title: Housing — Sunshine Coast
resources.body: Numbeo reported A$1,687.50 per month for a one-bedroom apartment in the city centre (updated 19 June 2026): https://www.numbeo.com/cost-of-living/in/Sunshine-Coast . Queensland's RTA caps a general-tenancy rental bond at four weeks' rent (represented as 1 month): https://www.rta.qld.gov.au/starting-a-tenancy/rental-bond . realestate.com.au lists Sunshine Coast rental properties: https://about.realestate.com.au/sitemap/queensland/

resources.title: Banking — Sunshine Coast
resources.body: ANZ says newcomers need key ID such as a passport, an Australian residential address, an Australian mobile number and a tax identification number or equivalent: https://www.anz.com.au/personal/bank-accounts/everyday-accounts/migrant-banking/ . CommBank requires an original current passport and foreign-tax-residency TINs, followed by branch identity verification after arrival: https://www.commbank.com.au/moving-to-australia/banking.html

resources.title: Schools & childcare — Sunshine Coast
resources.body: Matthew Flinders Anglican College in Buderim states that its Advanced Mathematics pathway includes preparation for Cambridge IGCSE examinations: https://www.mfac.edu.au/prospectus/welcome-to-our-school/ . The Queensland Department of Education Schools Directory can be searched by school name or suburb: https://schoolsdirectory.eq.edu.au/

resources.title: Registration & admin — Sunshine Coast
resources.body: Sunshine Coast arrivals enter Australia through Sunshine Coast Airport or Brisbane Airport, where under Australian law most passengers must identify themselves and complete an Incoming Passenger Card (IPC); the Australian Border Force provides the card on board or in the arrival terminal, it must be completed in English, and prescribed exemptions apply: https://www.abf.gov.au/entering-and-leaving-australia/crossing-the-border/at-the-border/incoming-passenger-card-(ipc)

resources.title: Tax & finance — Sunshine Coast
resources.body: A foreign-passport holder who is in Australia with a valid work-rights visa can apply free online for a Tax File Number through the ATO Individual Auto-Registration system: https://www.ato.gov.au/individuals-and-families/tax-file-number/apply-for-a-tfn/foreign-passport-holders-permanent-migrants-and-temporary-visitors-tfn-application

resources.title: Transport — Sunshine Coast
resources.body: Translink is the Sunshine Coast public-transport network; fares are A$0.50 per journey and a visitor go explore card provides unlimited Sunshine Coast bus travel for A$1.50 per day, but no monthly-pass price was published: https://translink.com.au/travel-with-us/around-queensland/sunshine-coast . Resident-visa holders must transfer to a Queensland licence after living in Queensland for 3 months; requirements depend on the issuing country and may include tests: https://www.qld.gov.au/transport/licensing/driver-licensing/overseas/transfer . Eligible residents can enrol in Medicare online through myGov or with a Medicare enrolment form, using a current passport or ImmiCard and valid Home Affairs visa details: https://www.servicesaustralia.gov.au/enrolling-medicare?context=60092

resources.title: Housing — Sydney
resources.body: Sydney is Australia's most expensive rental market. A 1-bedroom apartment in the city centre (CBD) typically rents for approximately AUD 600–700 per week. The standard bond (deposit) is 4 weeks rent, as regulated by NSW Fair Trading. Primary rental portals are realestate.com.au and domain.com.au.

resources.title: Banking — Sydney
resources.body: To open a bank account in Australia, new arrivals typically need a valid passport, proof of Australian address, and a Tax File Number (TFN). CommBank allows account opening up to 14 days before arrival and accepts new migrants within 12 months of arrival with in-branch ID verification. ANZ and NAB also offer accounts for new residents.

resources.title: Schools & childcare — Sydney
resources.body: Sydney has a wide range of international schools offering IB (International Baccalaureate), British curriculum, and American curriculum. The national school directory myschool.edu.au lists all Australian schools including international-curriculum institutions.

resources.title: Registration & admin — Sydney
resources.body: Visa holders in Australia must notify the Department of Home Affairs (Home Affairs) of any address changes. New residents should register with myGov (my.gov.au) to link essential government services including the ATO (tax), Medicare, and Centrelink.

resources.title: Tax & finance — Sydney
resources.body: All workers and income earners in Australia require a Tax File Number (TFN) from the Australian Taxation Office (ATO). You can apply for a TFN online for free at ato.gov.au. The TFN is used by employers for payroll tax and by the ATO for income tax returns.

resources.title: Transport — Sydney
resources.body: Sydney's public transport is operated by Transport for NSW using the Opal card system (tap-on/tap-off). Fares are distance-based with a weekly travel cap applying after 8 paid journeys. The Opal daily cap and weekly cap provide cost savings for frequent travellers. Overseas licence holders may drive in NSW on their overseas licence; exchange to an NSW licence is required after becoming a NSW resident (no fixed time limit but must be done when intending to reside permanently). Medicare registration for eligible visa holders is via Services Australia (servicesaustralia.gov.au).

resources.title: Housing — Wollongong
resources.body: Numbeo's July 2026 Wollongong data reports AUD 1,430 per month for a one-bedroom city-centre apartment; NSW caps a rental bond at four weeks' rent, represented as one month here; realestate.com.au is Australia's leading property resource and provides a Wollongong rental search.

resources.title: Banking — Wollongong
resources.body: Newcomer options supported by official bank pages include CommBank and ANZ Plus. ANZ Plus requires a passport, selfie, Australian mobile number and Australian residential address; CommBank's arrival setup requires its welcome letter, the first two pages of the Visa Grant notice, the original current passport and foreign tax-residency TINs.

resources.title: Schools & childcare — Wollongong
resources.body: The Illawarra Grammar School in the Wollongong region offers invitation-only Cambridge IGCSE Co-ordinated Sciences and Global Perspectives; the NSW Public School Finder is the official directory for local and nearby public schools.

resources.title: Registration & admin — Wollongong
resources.body: Most passengers entering Australia must complete and present an Incoming Passenger Card, including their intended Australian address; the responsible authority is the Australian Border Force.

resources.title: Tax & finance — Wollongong
resources.body: A permanent migrant or temporary visitor who is in Australia and holds a valid work-rights visa can apply free online for a Tax File Number through the Australian Taxation Office's Individual Auto-Registration system.

resources.title: Transport — Wollongong
resources.body: Wollongong is in the Illawarra Opal network. No monthly pass is published; adult pay-as-you-go travel is capped at AUD 50 per week. Australian citizens, permanent residents and New Zealand licence holders must transfer an overseas licence within three months; temporary overseas visitors arriving after 1 July 2023 may use an overseas licence for up to six months. Eligible permanent residents can enrol in Medicare online through myGov or with a Medicare enrolment form.
